sections.content:
You know *ahora bien* ("that said") from the first lesson of this unit. Here it joins two phrases that soften an opposition instead of cancelling what came before:

• *eso sí*: "mind you", "but only if". You accept something and add a condition or a limit. It is conversational, and *sí* keeps its accent.
• *de todos modos* (also *de todas formas*): "anyway", "in any case". What you say or do stays the same whatever happens.
• *ahora bien*: more formal than *eso sí*. It raises a point that limits what you accepted.

All three keep the first idea true. What differs is what they add: *eso sí* adds a condition, *de todos modos* says that nothing changes, and *ahora bien* adds a limit.

sections.title: Three ways to soften
rows: Te presto el coche; eso sí, lo devuelves hoy.
I'll lend you the car; mind you, you bring it back today.
Dicen que va a llover; de todos modos, voy a ir.
They say it will rain; I'm going anyway.
Es un buen plan. Ahora bien, cuesta mucho.
It is a good plan. That said, it costs a lot.

sections.content: Do not mix up *eso sí* with *eso si*: without the accent, *si* means "if". *De todos modos* can also close a conversation, like the English "anyway".
